items.text: ReConTrace: Retrieval Consistency Analysis for Hallucination and Memory Contamination in Long-Term LLM Agents

Sepyan Purnama Kristanto**, Lutfi Hakim*, Dianni Yusuf*, Moh Erdda Habibi⁺, Junaedi Adi Prasetyo+ * *Department of Software Engineering Technology, Politeknik Negeri Banyuwangi, Banyuwangi, Indonesia Email: {sepyan.kristanto, lutfi, dianniyusuf}@poliwangi.ac.id Department of Informatics, Bina Nusantara University, Jakarta, Indonesia Email: moh.erdda@binus.ac.id Department of Electrical Engineering, Digital Telecommunications Network Program, Politeknik Negeri Malang, Malang, Indonesia Email: junaedi.prasetyo@polinema.ac.id

Abstract-Long-horizon LLM agents rely on episodic retrieval- augmented memory. Two failure modes compound: intrinsic hallucination and memory contamination. Errors written back into memory cause cascading epistemic decay. We propose RECONTRACE, a reference-free framework that detects and attributes both failures in real time. It combines dual-query probing with a Three-Partition Consistency Graph (TPCG) over queries, memory chunks, and atomic claims. Contradiction- attenuated edge weights yield a normalized graph Laplacian whose Fiedler eigenvalue X₂ quantifies retrieval coherence. A cal- ibrated logistic classifier maps spectral and provenance features to four states: Clean (C₀), Hallucination (C₁), Temporal (C₂), or Cross-Session (C₃). Reflection poisoning is an ingestion pathway, not a class. On LONGAGENT-RECONBENCH (1,200 trajectories, k=0.84), RECONTRACE reaches AUROC 0.942 (F1 90.0%) on contamination and 0.938 (F1 88.6%) on hallucination detection- +10.4 pp AUROC over SelfCheckGPT-at 64.2 ms per turn, zero extra LLM calls. Active memory purification raises 100-turn task success from 63.8% to 89.2%.
Index Terms-Long-term LLM agents, episodic memory, hallu- cination detection, memory contamination, spectral graph theory, retrieval consistency.
I. INTRODUCTION

LLM-based autonomous agents increasingly run long- horizon tasks in healthcare, law, and public administration [1], [2]. Because context windows are finite, they externalise conversational history into episodic vector memory [3], [4]. Each turn: retrieve top-k chunks by cosine similarity [5], then generate Yₜ from them. This architecture is vulnerable. Two failure modes corrupt reasoning: (1) Intrinsic Hallucination- claims contradicting the retrieved context, from decoding noise or parametric bias [6], [7]; (2) Memory Contamination- stored chunks now obsolete, contradictory, or cross-pollinated from other sessions [8], [9]. Self-reflection compounds both: erroneous Yₜ written back to memory becomes future ground truth [2], [4], [10], [11], causing monotonic epistemic decay (Fig. 1(a)).

Existing detectors (SELFCHECKGPT [12], FACTSCORE [13]) assume a single static turn. They cannot separate confabulation from reasoning over a corrupted store-and multi-sample consistency costs 3-5 extra LLM calls per turn.

To address these limitations, we present RECONTRACE (Retrieval Consistency Trace), an external-reference-free framework for real-time failure detection and attribution (Fig. 1(b)), organized around two research questions:
RQ1: Can retrieval contamination and intrinsic hallucina- tion be topologically distinguished without any external reference corpus?
RQ2: How reliably does contradiction-attenuated spec- tral connectivity (X₂) predict downstream agent memory stability?
Our primary contributions are:
Three-Partition Consistency Graph (TPCG): Query probes, retrieved chunks, and atomic claims are orga- nized into a three-partition graph with non-negative, contradiction-attenuated edge weights.
Spectral Coherence Metric: Retrieval contamination creates topological bottlenecks in the TPCG, detectable via the Fiedler eigenvalue X₂ of its normalized Laplacian.
Failure-Origin Attribution: A calibrated logistic classi- fier over spectral and provenance features distinguishes C₀₋C₃ epistemic states.

We evaluate on LONGAGENT-RECONBENCH-1,200 tra- jectories / 81,370 chunks across four domains, 12 specialist annotators (K=0.84): RECONTRACE outperforms all seven baselines at 64.2 ms/turn (zero extra LLM calls) and raises 100-turn task success by +25.4 pp.
II. RELATED WORK
A. Hallucination Detection in LLMs

FACTSCORE [13] verifies atomic claims against Wikipedia; SELFCHECKGPT [12] measures cross-sample consistency. All assume a static single-turn context: when retrieved context it- self is corrupted, they cannot distinguish internal confabulation from faithful reasoning over a contaminated store.
B. Memory Security in Agentic Systems

MemGPT [2], MemoryBank [3], and Reflexion [4] establish foundational agent memory. AgentPoison [10], BadAgent [9], Pulipaka et al. [11], and MemSecBench [8] target adversarial poisoning and repair. RECONTRACE instead addresses non- adversarial epistemic drift without ground-truth labels at infer- ence time.
C. RAG Robustness and Knowledge-Conflict Resolution

FLARE [14] retrieves on demand, Self-RAG [15] critiques its own passages, and Astute RAG [16] resolves knowledge conflicts-all within one turn over an immutable corpus. RECONTRACE complements them by auditing the retrieval substrate across turns and routing to mode-specific repairs (invalidation, re-scoping, regeneration) rather than uniform re- retrieval.
D. Spectral Graph Methods in NLP

Spectral graph theory underpins clustering and community detection in language data [17], [18]. The Fiedler eigenvalue X₂ [19] bounds conductance via Cheeger's inequality [20]. Graph-RAG [21] uses knowledge graphs for summarization; Binkowski et al. [22] apply spectral attention features to detect hallucination in single-turn LLM outputs. We extend spectral analysis to the heterogeneous retrieval-interaction manifold, directly linking X₂ to multi-turn epistemic integrity.

2) Epistemic Failure Taxonomy: We define four mutually exclusive epistemic states for agent output Yₜ:
C₀ (Clean): Yₜ is factually grounded and supported by uncontaminated chunks in Mₜ.
C₁ (Intrinsic Hallucination): Yₜ contains assertions that are unsupported by, or that contradict, valid retrieved chunks, owing to decoding error or parametric bias.
C₂ (Temporal Contamination): Yₜ is grounded in chunks m ε Mₜₖ that were accurate at ingestion time Tₘ but have since been invalidated by world-state updates.
C₃ (Cross-Session Contamination): Yₜ is tainted by chunks from a semantically unrelated session that collide in the embedding space.
Reflection Poisoning as a Provenance Pathway. We do not

treat reflection poisoning as a separate epistemic state. Instead, it is the ingestion mechanism through which a C₁ hallucination is written into Mₜ and subsequently retrieved as C₂ or C₃ contamination in later turns.

Scope of the C₂ definition. RECONTRACE detects internal inconsistency-a chunk contradicted by a more recent one. It does not certify world state. Evaluation scores this signal against the simulation's update log-the ground truth for temporal invalidity (Table I).
